source: CAMFAD student thesis: "Establishment of a New Coconut Plantation Farm", National School of Agriculture, July 1994
text:
Seedlings selected for transplanting into the field should be about 12-18 months old. Careful handling during transplant is stressed: the root ball/soil around the roots should be kept intact to avoid root damage, and workers digging the transplant holes and moving seedlings should be careful and experienced so as not to injure the young palm.

Planting-hole size: approximately 60 x 60 cm.

Spacing/layout: this thesis specifies a triangular (staggered/offset) planting pattern with roughly 9 meters between planting points in each direction, illustrated with a diamond/triangular-lattice diagram of planting points. At this 9-meter triangular spacing, the thesis states that one hectare can accommodate approximately 143 coconut trees. This triangular layout gives a higher planting density per hectare than a simple square grid at the same inter-tree distance, and reflects a different spacing recommendation from other sources in this knowledge base that describe a 10 x 10 meter square grid (see the AIDOC farmer leaflet's planting_hole_prep_and_spacing topic) — farmers should be aware both spacing approaches exist in the literature and choose based on their own land, variety, and management capacity.
